study type: Secondary data analysis of the National Family Health Survey (NFHS)
exposure: Educational level of the head of the household
cohort: Nationally representative sample of 230,870 women in India from the 2019-21 NFHS
finding: The study found a significant increase in CS deliveries in India, with higher odds observed among women with higher education, more ANC visits, higher wealth, urban residence, higher partner education, and supportive partners.
mod_finding: The odds of both elective and emergency CS were significantly higher among women from richer families.
